scope: Fake/local deterministic callback lifetime and atomic report custody
pass_rule: Both fresh attempts exit 0 and satisfy all listed invariants. No product reliability claim.
prior_attempt: R06 ran normal and optimized once each but failed its test assertions because it incorrectly expected call_id in the successful observation report and called unsupported interface_close on the one-shot server. It did observe the caller timeout and later Future response; R06 remains failed and is not pooled.
invariants: wait until exact callback Future returns TimeoutError at 8 seconds and verify it remains pending;
read its exact call ID from the read-only interface_results call list before release;
release callback once, then await the same future <=30s;
require one observer invocation, exact finalized report, no .tmp file, and exact result readback;
no dispatch, task effect, input, replay, retries, or replacements;
fixture teardown only after future completion.
question: In the same controlled 8s callback timeout experiment, does exact call-list lookup (the returned observation report omits call_id) allow verification that the single pending observation finishes, its same-call raw report is atomically finalized, and teardown occurs only after the Future drains?
